Anna — thanks for the note and the worksheet. We can definitely support a blended CapEx/OpEx invoicing approach; many enterprise customers use it for CFO sign-off and capitalization. Quick answers up front:

- Blended invoicing: yes — we can issue an upfront invoice for the prepay portion (suitable for capitalization) and then monthly/quarterly invoices for the remaining OpEx commitments.
- Term discounts: for a 3-year commit with a 40% upfront prepay in year 1, we typically model a 15–22% effective discount depending on total committed USD and payment timing.
- Pro forma: attached is a budgetary pro forma for the scenario you described (assumes usage bands from your worksheet).

I've attached a draft quote and pro forma invoice for the team to review. Karthik (cc'd) will align on commercial terms and can run exact unit economics if you want a breakdown by model-class/token.

Next steps proposed:
1) Karthik to confirm final committed USD and any sequencing constraints by Wed EOD.
2) We issue an updated pro forma and a draft SOW (if needed).
3) If acceptable, we generate an invoice for the 40% prepay and provide the payment instructions.

Team / Anna — thanks for the context. High level proposal below; I'm attaching a pricing worksheet that lays out the USD numbers.

Proposal (budgetary):
- Term: 3 years (FY29–FY31)
- Year 1: 40% prepay of the committed annual spend (invoice issued at signing, suitable for capitalization).
- Years 2–3: annual OpEx top-ups invoiced annually in advance (or quarterly if preferred).
- Effective discount: 18% off list for the blended structure (breakdown: 12% term discount + additional 6% early payment / prepay credit).
- Ramp schedule suggestion: 60% of committed capacity available in Q1–Q2 (to allow integration), 80% by Q3, 100% by Q4. We can front-load credits if they need steady-state earlier.

Commercial notes:
- We will provide an invoice template that clearly states "Capitalizable prepaid services" line item.
- We can include a 30-day credit-hold clause for late OpEx payments, and a right-to-scale-back clause for sustained underutilization (standard for multi-year prepay).

Attachments: Redwood_FY29_CapEx_OpEx_Blend_Quote_v2.xlsx (xlsx)
